claims.text: POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails on the driver's own trace. EV-GPS-09104 places every one of the driver's 37 fixes at 559.3707 m from the pickup pin — min_distance_m, mean_distance_m and max_distance_m are identical — and the derived arrival block reports qualifying_fix_count 0, meaning not a single fix fell inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius that POL-NS-02 takes from fee_schedule.arrival_radius_m. The driver was never inside the pickup geofence at or before his 07:25:20 'arrived' event, so the conjunctive test in POL-NS-01 is broken and the SGD 4.00 fee is not chargeable.

POL-NS-01 limb (c) fails independently, so breaking (b) is not even necessary. The longest continuous in-geofence run in the trace is 0.0 seconds (longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec, fix_count 0), against the 300 second minimum for the STANDARD zone class, a measured shortfall of 300 seconds. Limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the 'arrived' tap, and no qualifying fix ever occurred — so the marker never ripened into a chargeable no-show.

Under POL-NS-02 the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes preceding the 07:31:00 driver cancellation, so the driver is not deemed to have arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. EV-FARE-09104 itemises that fee at SGD 4.00 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the sum to be returned to the filing rider is SGD 4.00.

POL-NS-05 applies squarely on the arrival marker itself. At the 07:25:20 'arrived' timestamp the trace puts the driver 559.3707 m from the pin — far beyond the clause's 300 m threshold — so the marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock. Recomputing the clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix yields none (qualifying_fix_count 0), which is POL-NS-05(ii): the fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip must be recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list. The driver's own statement that he 'marked arrival and waited' is contradicted by his own trace.

POL-NS-06 makes the refund unconditional on this record. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds against the 300 second STANDARD minimum — a 300 second shortfall — so the cancellation fee 'is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.' Any suggestion that the state of the rider's own device excuses the charge is foreclosed by the clause's express terms; the waiting period is the consideration the fee was taken for.

POL-NS-03 cannot rescue the fee either, and the driver cannot convert this into a wrong-entrance case. The clause's entire test is that the driver held position 'not more than 400 m from the pickup pin'; here the driver's stationary fixes sit at 559.3707 m (min = mean = max), outside the 400 m ceiling. The wrong-entrance route — and with it any pin-ambiguity goodwill payment under POL-NS-03(ii) — is unavailable, and the refund stands at full.

POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable to the driver on the face of the trace: the derived accumulation block records run_count 0 and accumulated_sec 0.0, so there are no separate in-geofence intervals to sum in the first place. The waiting window also carries no advisory at all — EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, and a MISSING advisory cannot meet the limb's 'present and populated' requirement. I disclose that artifact's impairment expressly. Nothing on this record repairs the 300 second shortfall.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is met, so the case should be decided on its merits rather than held: the apparent tension between the driver's self-reported marker and the GPS is not an unresolved contradiction, because POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-02 resolve it on the clauses' own terms. The citable profile counters are clean — rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires, and both rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so POL-NS-09(c) does not fire. Every artifact relied on above is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence floor is not engaged and the money can move now.

claims.text: The amount is not in dispute on the arithmetic, and the rider gains nothing there: SGD 4.00 is exactly what the fee schedule produces for this trip. The STANDARD zone-class fee is SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee is SGD 4.00; the resolution rule takes the GREATER of the two, which is the SGD 4.00 cancellation_fee line, and the fare breakdown's total_charged of SGD 4.00 reconciles with it. There is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect for the rider to exploit, so if any clause makes the fee chargeable, the amount is already right.

On the trip record's own facts, two of POL-NS-01's four limbs hold. Limb (a): the record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-04T07:25:20+08:00. Limb (d): the record shows no boarding (started_at is null) and the trip is terminated by the driver at 07:31:00 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes the limb recognises, which is 5 minutes 40 seconds after the marker and therefore at or after a STANDARD 300-second dwell on that timeline. The dispute consequently turns entirely on the two GPS-derived limbs, (b) and (c).

The rider's exonerating route under POL-NS-04 cannot run on this record. Limb (a) fails at the threshold, because the chat log contains no rider message at all: its only two messages are the system arrival notice at 07:25:21 and the driver's own 'I have marked arrival.' at 07:25:40. Limb (c) is independently unsatisfied: the rider track's 17 fixes sit a uniform 519.46 m from the registered pickup pin VEN-BP-180 at a constant reported speed of 0.0, with rider_qualifying_fix_count of 0, far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius the limb requires for the majority of qualifying fixes.

I do not stretch the decisive GPS point, I concede it. The driver's own trace places him a uniform 559.37 m from the pickup pin on every one of its 37 fixes, stationary at a reported speed of 0.0, with qualifying_fix_count of 0 and a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 0 seconds. That is more than half a kilometre outside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and beyond even the 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling in POL-NS-03, so POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) fail on this record, and no POL-NS-06 accumulation is open to rescue the dwell: EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), so there is no traffic advisory covering this pickup road and no second in-geofence interval to add. On the GPS record alone the fee is not chargeable.

The one question this record does not settle by itself is which of the platform's two accounts of the arrival is authoritative, and that is the POL-NS-09(b) question. EV-TRIP-09104 records the driver 'arrived' at 07:25:20 with a wait_time_min of 5.7, and the platform broadcast that same assertion to the rider as the system message 'Your driver has arrived' at 07:25:21 in EV-CHAT-09104; EV-GPS-09104 places the driver 559.37 m from the pin throughout the same interval, with a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds. Both artifacts are admissible at weight 1.0, neither is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d), and the driver's position is carried by the trace alone, with no per-fix horizontal accuracy in the bundle against which the 25 m filter can be checked independently. POL-NS-05 tells the Judge what follows if the trace is taken as authoritative on position, but it presumes the very point in issue. If the Judge treats the conflict as unresolved, the disputed SGD 4.00 should be HELD under POL-NS-09 rather than refunded while the reviewer settles which record is right; an escalated fee is held, not returned.

ruling.explanation: To both parties. The SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-09104 is refunded in full to the rider. The fee can stand only if all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold, and two of them fail on the platform's own measurements. EV-GPS-09104 places the driver's vehicle 559.37 m from the registered pickup pin VEN-BP-180 on every one of its 37 fixes (min_distance_m = mean_distance_m = max_distance_m), with qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest continuous in-geofence run of 0.0 seconds. The driver was therefore never inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival geofence at or before the 07:25:20 'arrived' event — limb (b) fails — and never accumulated any of the 300-second minimum dwell — limb (c) fails. The trip record's own 'arrived' event and 5.7-minute wait figure cannot repair that: under POL-NS-05 a marker set while the trace puts the driver more than 300 m from the pin is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock, which is recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix; there was none. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies directly: full refund, no driver compensation, and the trip recorded as a false-arrival event — that last is the referral above. The same result follows independently under POL-NS-02 (no qualifying in-radius fix → the driver never arrived) and POL-NS-06 (0-second dwell against a 300-second minimum → the fee is refunded whether or not the rider was present or responded). The driver's argument that the gap between the trip record and the GPS must be escalated under POL-NS-09(b) is rejected: that trigger requires that no clause resolves the conflict, and POL-NS-05 is exactly the clause that resolves it. The remaining POL-NS-09 triggers were checked and do not fire — the confidence floor is not engaged, the citable counters are clean (rider no_show_disputes_30d 0; disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 on both profiles), and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming test on the driver's trailing-30-day figures (1 termination against 120 completed trips) is nowhere near its thresholds, so no compensation is in issue. On the money itself there is no fare defect: the SGD 4.00 line equals the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), so POL-NS-08(d) is satisfied and the whole contested amount is what is refunded. The wrong-entrance route in POL-NS-03 cannot rescue the charge — it is confined to a driver stationary within 400 m of the pin, and this driver was at 559.37 m — so no pin-ambiguity goodwill arises. The rider's own track (519.46 m from the pin) and the absence of any rider chat message mean POL-NS-04 cannot be run, but that is immaterial, because the refund under POL-NS-05(ii)/POL-NS-02/POL-NS-06 does not depend on where the rider was. Finally, traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); it carries no fact and forecloses any dwell accumulation under POL-NS-06(i), but it does not affect the refund. Neither party's profile was used as a ground of decision.
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii): record trip TRP-09104 as a FALSE-ARRIVAL event against driver DRV-09104 — the 'arrived' marker was set at 2026-09-04T07:25:20+08:00 while EV-GPS-09104 placed the vehicle 559.37 m from the pickup pin, and no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip.

ruling.explanation:
Rider: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to you in full. Driver: no compensation is payable, and the trip is referred for a false-arrival record against you.

Why the fee does not stand. POL-NS-01 charges a no-show fee only if all four conditions hold together. Two hold: the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 07:25:20 (limb (a)), and it shows no boarding with the trip terminated by the driver under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. Two fail. Limb (b) requires the GPS trace to place you inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at or before that event, and every one of the 37 fixes in EV-GPS-09104 sits 559.37 m from pin VEN-BP-180 — qualifying_fix_count 0. Limb (c) requires 300 seconds of continuous in-geofence dwell, measured from the first qualifying fix and not from the tap; the longest qualifying run is 0.0 seconds, a 300 second shortfall. Because the test is conjunctive, the fee is not chargeable (POL-NS-02; POL-NS-06), and the rider's claims on limbs (b) and (c) are accepted.

The driver's account does not change that. The 'arrived' marker, the wait_time_min of 5.7, and 'I marked arrival and waited before cancelling' are all assertions about the tap, and POL-NS-01 measures the dwell from GPS entry into the geofence, not from the tap. POL-NS-05 makes the position decisive: a marker set 559.37 m from the pin — over 300 m — is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock. With no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) gives the full refund, no compensation, and the false-arrival referral above.

POL-NS-03 cannot rescue the fee: its wrong-entrance route requires the driver to have held position within 400 m of the pin, and 559.37 m is outside that ceiling, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill is also unavailable. POL-NS-04 does not apply — the chat log carries no rider message at all, and the rider track's 17 fixes sit 519.46 m out. POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is closed off: there are no in-geofence intervals to sum (run_count 0), and the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-09104-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so it cannot be 'present and populated'.

On the driver's POL-NS-09(b) argument: I do not treat the record as holding an unresolved contradiction. The apparent conflict between the self-reported marker and the trace is precisely the situation POL-NS-05 exists to resolve, and it resolves it on its own terms by making the GPS position authoritative and voiding the marker; the 'Your driver has arrived' system notice in EV-CHAT-09104 is generated from the same driver tap, so it is not an independent account of position. No other escalation trigger fires: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the citable counters are clean (rider no_show_disputes_30d 0; disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 on both sides; driver no_show_terminations_30d 1 against the POL-NS-07 threshold of 4), and no deciding artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)-(d) — the trace has 100% coverage, 37 fixes, no gaps, and the fare line of SGD 4.00 reconciles with the resolution rule.

On confidence: the fact that decides this case — that the driver was never inside the pickup geofence — is carried by EV-GPS-09104 at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0. The MISSING advisory at weight 0.0 carries no deciding fact; its absence is cited only to show that POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable.

ruling.explanation:
Rider, your claim is upheld in full: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to you. Driver, the fee fails on your own track, for reasons that do not depend on the rider's word at all.

POL-NS-01 needs all four conditions. Two of yours hold on the trip record (EV-TRIP-09104): there is an 'arrived' event at 07:25:20, and the trip was ended by you at 07:31:00 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding. Limbs (b) and (c) fail. Your GPS trace (EV-GPS-09104) places all 37 of your fixes at 559.37 m from the pickup pin — min, mean and max identical — at a constant 0.0 km/h, so you were never inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius that POL-NS-02 takes from the fee schedule, and your longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum.

POL-NS-02: with no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before the 07:31:00 cancellation, you are not deemed to have arrived, limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund.

POL-NS-05: at your 07:25:20 arrival tap the trace puts you 559.37 m from the pin, past the clause's 300 m trigger, so the marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock. Recomputing the clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix yields none, which is POL-NS-05(ii): full refund, no driver compensation, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event — that instruction is carried in the referrals above.

POL-NS-06: the effective dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a 300-second shortfall, so the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded.

POL-NS-03 does not rescue the fee and produces no pin-ambiguity goodwill: its wrong-entrance route requires you to have held position within 400 m of the pin, and your stationary fixes sit at 559.37 m, outside that ceiling.

The Driver Advocate's POL-NS-09(b) escalation argument is rejected. There is no unresolved contradiction for a reviewer to settle: POL-NS-05 exists precisely to resolve a self-set arrival marker against an authoritative GPS position, and it resolves this one. The status you set records only that you set it, and your statement that you 'marked arrival and waited' is contradicted by your own trace, which shows no motion and no fix nearer than 559.37 m at any point. No other escalation trigger is met — both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (1 termination against 120 completed trips in 30 days).

The rider's own track places the rider's device 519.46 m from the pin with 0 qualifying fixes, and no locating message was sent, so POL-NS-04 does not apply — but that changes nothing, because the refund follows from POL-NS-02, POL-NS-05(ii) and POL-NS-06 independently of the rider's position. The rider's GPS-only claims and the driver's concession that the trace shows no in-geofence fix agree on the decisive point.

Amount: SGD 4.00, the whole contested sum. The fare breakdown's cancellation_fee line (SGD 4.00) equals the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee, both SGD 4.00, and total_charged is SGD 4.00, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and nothing further to reconcile. No driver compensation is payable.
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii): record trip TRP-09104 as a false-arrival event against driver DRV-09104 — the 'arrived' marker was tapped at 2026-09-04T07:25:20+08:00 while the GPS trace (EV-GPS-09104) places the driver 559.37 m from the pickup pin VEN-BP-180, and no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip.

ruling.explanation:
Outcome: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider. Both of your accounts are on the record and they disagree about the arrival, but the no-show policy itself says which one decides that question, so this case can be settled now rather than sent to a reviewer.

DRIVER — Two of the four conditions in POL-NS-01 fail, and both are measured from the GPS trace, not from the 'arrived' tap. Limb (b) requires the trace to place you inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at or before the arrival event; EV-GPS-09104 puts every one of your 37 fixes at 559.37 m from the pin (min = mean = max), with qualifying_fix_count 0. Limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of 300 seconds measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix; the longest qualifying run is 0.0 seconds. The fee is therefore not chargeable and is refunded. POL-NS-02 reaches the same result (no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before the 07:31:00 cancellation), and POL-NS-06 independently makes the refund unconditional on a 0-second dwell against a 300-second minimum, whether or not the rider was present or responding.

Your 'arrived' marker at 07:25:20 was set while the trace placed you more than 300 m from the pin, so POL-NS-05 treats it as FALSE; because there is no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) directs a full refund, no compensation, and that the trip be recorded as a false-arrival event — that referral is included above. POL-NS-03 cannot assist you: its whole test is stationary fixes within 400 m of the pin, and your stationary fixes sit at 559 m, outside that ceiling, so no pin-ambiguity goodwill arises. POL-NS-07 compensation is not payable because it requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, which it is not. On the amount you are right — SGD 4.00 is exactly what the fee schedule produces for a STANDARD zone / RYDE_X trip, and there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect — but the amount being correct does not make the fee chargeable. EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and is disclosed as such: its absence makes POL-NS-06(i) accumulation unavailable, and I have not used it against you beyond that.

Your escalation argument under POL-NS-09(b) is rejected. The tension you identify is real — the trip record says 'arrived' while the trace puts you over half a kilometre away — but a clause does resolve it: POL-NS-05 says a self-reported arrival marker does not start the clock where the trace places the driver more than 300 m out, and POL-NS-01(b) and (c) are defined by the trace rather than the tap. POL-NS-09(b) requires that no clause resolves the conflict; here one does, so the fee is not held. No other escalation trigger fires: POL-NS-09(c) needs 2 or more same-pair no-show disputes in 90 days (both are 0), POL-NS-09(d) needs no_show_disputes_30d of 3 or more (it is 0) or the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check (no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4), and POL-NS-09(e) is not met because the deciding trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and is not impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d) — coverage 100%, 37 fixes at the expected 10-second cadence, no gaps, rider track present.

RIDER — You receive the whole contested SGD 4.00; nothing is deducted. Your point that POL-NS-04 does not run (no rider message in the chat log, and the rider track's 17 fixes sit 519.46 m out at rider_qualifying_fix_count 0) is accepted but does not matter here: the refund comes from POL-NS-01(b)/(c), POL-NS-02, POL-NS-05(ii) and POL-NS-06, not from POL-NS-04. Your reading of the escalation triggers is also accepted.

CONFIDENCE — The deciding fact (the driver was never inside the arrival geofence) is carried by EV-GPS-09104 at weight 1.0, and the amount by EV-FARE-09104 at weight 1.0; the cap is therefore 1.0 and the platform floor of 0.70 is not engaged. A modest discount is taken for the absence of per-fix accuracy figures in the bundle, giving confidence 0.90.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails on the driver's own trace. EV-GPS-09104 places every one of the driver's 37 fixes at 559.3707 m from the pickup pin — min_distance_m, mean_distance_m and max_distance_m are identical — and the derived arrival block reports qualifying_fix_count 0, meaning not a single fix fell inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius that POL-NS-02 takes from fee_schedule.arrival_radius_m. The driver was never inside the pickup geofence at or before his 07:25:20 'arrived' event, so the conjunctive test in POL-NS-01 is broken and the SGD 4.00 fee is not chargeable.

POL-NS-01 limb (c) fails independently, so breaking (b) is not even necessary. The longest continuous in-geofence run in the trace is 0.0 seconds (longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec, fix_count 0), against the 300 second minimum for the STANDARD zone class, a measured shortfall of 300 seconds. Limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the 'arrived' tap, and no qualifying fix ever occurred — so the marker never ripened into a chargeable no-show.

Under POL-NS-02 the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes preceding the 07:31:00 driver cancellation, so the driver is not deemed to have arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. EV-FARE-09104 itemises that fee at SGD 4.00 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the sum to be returned to the filing rider is SGD 4.00.

POL-NS-05 applies squarely on the arrival marker itself. At the 07:25:20 'arrived' timestamp the trace puts the driver 559.3707 m from the pin — far beyond the clause's 300 m threshold — so the marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock. Recomputing the clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix yields none (qualifying_fix_count 0), which is POL-NS-05(ii): the fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip must be recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list. The driver's own statement that he 'marked arrival and waited' is contradicted by his own trace.

POL-NS-06 makes the refund unconditional on this record. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds against the 300 second STANDARD minimum — a 300 second shortfall — so the cancellation fee 'is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.' Any suggestion that the state of the rider's own device excuses the charge is foreclosed by the clause's express terms; the waiting period is the consideration the fee was taken for.

POL-NS-03 cannot rescue the fee either, and the driver cannot convert this into a wrong-entrance case. The clause's entire test is that the driver held position 'not more than 400 m from the pickup pin'; here the driver's stationary fixes sit at 559.3707 m (min = mean = max), outside the 400 m ceiling. The wrong-entrance route — and with it any pin-ambiguity goodwill payment under POL-NS-03(ii) — is unavailable, and the refund stands at full.

POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable to the driver on the face of the trace: the derived accumulation block records run_count 0 and accumulated_sec 0.0, so there are no separate in-geofence intervals to sum in the first place. The waiting window also carries no advisory at all — EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, and a MISSING advisory cannot meet the limb's 'present and populated' requirement. I disclose that artifact's impairment expressly. Nothing on this record repairs the 300 second shortfall.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is met, so the case should be decided on its merits rather than held: the apparent tension between the driver's self-reported marker and the GPS is not an unresolved contradiction, because POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-02 resolve it on the clauses' own terms. The citable profile counters are clean — rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires, and both rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so POL-NS-09(c) does not fire. Every artifact relied on above is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence floor is not engaged and the money can move now.

The amount is not in dispute on the arithmetic, and the rider gains nothing there: SGD 4.00 is exactly what the fee schedule produces for this trip. The STANDARD zone-class fee is SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee is SGD 4.00; the resolution rule takes the GREATER of the two, which is the SGD 4.00 cancellation_fee line, and the fare breakdown's total_charged of SGD 4.00 reconciles with it. There is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect for the rider to exploit, so if any clause makes the fee chargeable, the amount is already right.

On the trip record's own facts, two of POL-NS-01's four limbs hold. Limb (a): the record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-04T07:25:20+08:00. Limb (d): the record shows no boarding (started_at is null) and the trip is terminated by the driver at 07:31:00 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes the limb recognises, which is 5 minutes 40 seconds after the marker and therefore at or after a STANDARD 300-second dwell on that timeline. The dispute consequently turns entirely on the two GPS-derived limbs, (b) and (c).

The rider's exonerating route under POL-NS-04 cannot run on this record. Limb (a) fails at the threshold, because the chat log contains no rider message at all: its only two messages are the system arrival notice at 07:25:21 and the driver's own 'I have marked arrival.' at 07:25:40. Limb (c) is independently unsatisfied: the rider track's 17 fixes sit a uniform 519.46 m from the registered pickup pin VEN-BP-180 at a constant reported speed of 0.0, with rider_qualifying_fix_count of 0, far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius the limb requires for the majority of qualifying fixes.

I do not stretch the decisive GPS point, I concede it. The driver's own trace places him a uniform 559.37 m from the pickup pin on every one of its 37 fixes, stationary at a reported speed of 0.0, with qualifying_fix_count of 0 and a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 0 seconds. That is more than half a kilometre outside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and beyond even the 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling in POL-NS-03, so POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) fail on this record, and no POL-NS-06 accumulation is open to rescue the dwell: EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), so there is no traffic advisory covering this pickup road and no second in-geofence interval to add. On the GPS record alone the fee is not chargeable.

The one question this record does not settle by itself is which of the platform's two accounts of the arrival is authoritative, and that is the POL-NS-09(b) question. EV-TRIP-09104 records the driver 'arrived' at 07:25:20 with a wait_time_min of 5.7, and the platform broadcast that same assertion to the rider as the system message 'Your driver has arrived' at 07:25:21 in EV-CHAT-09104; EV-GPS-09104 places the driver 559.37 m from the pin throughout the same interval, with a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds. Both artifacts are admissible at weight 1.0, neither is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d), and the driver's position is carried by the trace alone, with no per-fix horizontal accuracy in the bundle against which the 25 m filter can be checked independently. POL-NS-05 tells the Judge what follows if the trace is taken as authoritative on position, but it presumes the very point in issue. If the Judge treats the conflict as unresolved, the disputed SGD 4.00 should be HELD under POL-NS-09 rather than refunded while the reviewer settles which record is right; an escalated fee is held, not returned.
